text.intro:
The calibration, step by step: which filters it is built on, how the model is chosen and scored, what it responds to, how it is
corrected, and what comes out on filters that were never in training. Each step says what was done before, what is done now, and why,
with the chart behind it. 12,393 IMPROVE filters with thermal (TOR) EC; 233 Addis filters as the test set. No Addis filter
has thermal EC, so the Addis level stays a range, and no aethalometer data are used.
text.set:
**What we chose.** Every IMPROVE filter of lots 248 and 251 that has a spectrum and thermal (TOR) EC: 12,393 filters from
157 sites. Nothing is picked to resemble Addis. **Why.** Any subset chosen to look like Addis has to be chosen by something
measured on the filter, and that selects on the measurement's own error (step 4). **Before.** Sets picked to resemble Addis: 906
smoke-flagged filters, the 800 and 450 lowest in OC/EC, the 500 nearest spectral look-alikes, one set per season. Each was judged by how
close it brought the Addis intercept against HIPS to zero. **What it cannot do.** IMPROVE is a mostly rural and remote network. Its
median OC/EC is 5.5; even its six urban sites sit near 3, and Addis is near 1. 99 % of Addis
filters are below IMPROVE's 5th percentile of FTIR OC/EC.
text.model:
**What we chose.** Partial least squares on unscaled spectra, 18 components, cross-validated with **whole sites held out**: five
folds, and no site is ever in training and test together. **Why whole sites.** Addis is a site the calibration has never seen, so the
honest error is the error on unseen sites. **Before.** The calibration app deals filters into ten interleaved folds, so every test filter
has neighbours from its own site in training, and it picks the component count at the first minimum of that error. At 18 components the interleaved protocol reports a median error of 1.13 µg per filter and an RMSE of 3.57; with whole sites held out the same model gives 1.14 and 3.73. The whole-site RMSE is lowest at 17 components; the interleaved one keeps falling to 22. On this broad set the two schemes differ by a few per cent; on narrow sets such as the smoke-flagged one the gap was much larger.
**Why 18, and fixed.** It is the count that reproduces SPARTAN's published Addis values, and one fixed count keeps every comparison on the
same model. The count matters more than it looks: the calibration's response to thermal EC rises with it, 0.33 at 6,
0.64 at 12, 0.78 at 18 and 0.81 at 25 components, and cross-validation error on IMPROVE barely sees that.
text.score:
**What we chose.** Score against thermal EC on IMPROVE, on groups chosen by site or by the *previous* sample at the site.
**Why.** A filter picked because its own TOR EC is high, or its own TOR OC/EC is low, is more likely to be one where TOR happened to read
high, so FTIR looks low on it. **Before.** Two yardsticks, both misleading: the Addis intercept against HIPS / 10, which is mostly HIPS
compression (the Nov 10 offset page), and FTIR ÷ TOR on the "heavy, low-OC/EC" IMPROVE subset chosen by each filter's own TOR. **What
changed.** On that subset FTIR ÷ TOR is 0.78; chosen by the previous sample it is
0.91, and on the six urban IMPROVE sites 0.91. In the
lowest OC/EC bin the same filters read 0.62 of thermal EC when binned by TOR's own ratio and
1.54 when binned by FTIR's own.
text.response:
**What we found.** Across IMPROVE site means the calibration's prediction is 0.9 µg per filter plus
**0.78 × thermal EC** (0.70–0.84). It under-responds to EC and makes up the difference with a fixed offset: a
blank filter reads 2.2 µg. That is right at IMPROVE's usual loadings and low on heavy filters. **What we tried in
training.** Weighting toward heavy filters leaves the gain at 0.78 and only raises the offset (a blank then reads
4.3 µg, and light filters get worse). Adding blank filters at zero helps the low end (blank 1.3 µg)
and leaves the gain at 0.81. **What works.** Removing the offset and dividing by the gain, with both fitted on *other* sites:
gain 0.96 (0.85–1.04), the six urban IMPROVE sites from 0.91 to 1.02, heavy filters from
0.95 to 1.03, light filters from 1.27 to 0.98. **The cost.** The largest errors are scaled
up with everything else (RMSE 6.56 to 7.72); the median error is unchanged.
text.addis:
**What comes out at Addis.** The Addis filters were never used to fit or choose anything. The recalibration learned on
IMPROVE raises the raw calibration by × 1.25 at the median filter, which is × 1.13 on SPARTAN's published values (median
4.62 to 4.92 µg/m³).
Against HIPS as measured every version has a large negative intercept (-6.2 for the published
product), which is HIPS compression. Against linearised HIPS the published product reads
0.55x +0.01 and the recalibrated one
0.61x +0.00.
**What this is not.** No Addis filter has thermal EC. The recalibration corrects the loading part of the bias, checked on IMPROVE sites it
had not seen; it says nothing about whether Addis's composition adds to it. HIPS is optical, and its MAC at Addis is not known.
text.baselines:
**What a baseline is for.** A PTFE filter has its own broad spectrum under the aerosol's. Raw spectra leave it in; the spline
(AIRSpec) baseline fits and removes a smooth curve above 1425 cm⁻¹; VIBES models the filter from a bank of blanks, and the PTFE-anchored
version protects the broad continuum that EC itself produces. **The test.** The same 12,393 IMPROVE filters, 18 components, whole
sites held out, for each. **What it shows.** No baseline changes the calibration's response to thermal EC: 0.77 raw,
0.75 spline, 0.73 production VIBES, 0.76 PTFE-anchored VIBES.
Deflated VIBES, which removes smooth directions, lowers it to 0.60. The six urban IMPROVE sites read
0.90, 0.94, 0.88 and 0.88
of thermal EC as trained, and 0.97, 1.01, 0.96 and
0.95 after the same recalibration. Baselines differ a little in median error
(1.08 to 1.34 µg per filter) and not in the thing that limits Addis.
**Before.** The spline baseline looked like the largest single improvement because it moved the Addis intercept against HIPS from
-4.7 to -1.4 µg/m³. Against linearised HIPS the two
intercepts are +0.18 and +0.26: the difference was HIPS
compression meeting a calibration that reads Addis at 0.38 of HIPS / 10
(raw: 0.84).
